name: Peng Ren

papers.title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
papers.abstract:
High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, where successful interaction requires time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. This challenge becomes especially pronounced in badminton, as the shuttlecock follows highly nonlinear trajectories and each return requires tightly coordinated contact selection, racket control, and balance recovery within a short time window. Although human demonstrations offer valuable motion priors for such athletic skills, available badminton data is often limited and imperfect; meanwhile, purely task-driven reinforcement learning can optimize returns but tends to produce unnatural motions that are difficult to deploy on hardware.
To address these challenges, we present a three-stage hierarchical framework for athletic humanoid badminton that combines human motion priors with task-driven optimization. The framework first learns a compact latent skill space from retargeted human demonstrations, then optimizes skill composition through reinforcement learning, and finally regularizes the learned behavior with a context-conditioned adversarial latent prior to promote human-like motion. When deployed on a real humanoid robot, our system demonstrates multi-skill badminton play with human players, including rallies and jump smashes. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first real-world demonstration of humanoid jump-smash skills in racket sports.

papers.title: Closing the Loop in Humanoid VLA: Persistent 3D Object Tokens for Verifiable Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action policies are a promising foundation for general robot control, but long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation requires the robot to treat task objects as persistent physical entities across movement, contact, occlusion, and recovery. We study this problem as object-state divergence: the object state used to condition a whole-body action can differ from the state used to decide whether the action achieved the intended physical relation. We propose Persistent Object Tokenization (POT), which maintains role-indexed 3D object records from RGB-D observations and converts them into object tokens for a whole-body action expert. Instantiated as POT-VLA, the same object records condition action generation and support geometric predicate checks, yielding a closed-loop execution system in which object state is both actionable and verifiable. On a Unitree G1, POT-VLA improves a matched direct GR00T-N1.7 baseline from 39/80 to 71/80 successes over eight real-world task families. In an external Being-0-aligned reference, POT-VLA achieves 44/50 successes on aligned service tasks, compared with the 37/50 success reported by the Being-0 paper. The largest gains occur on tasks requiring maintained 3D relations, suggesting that persistent object-centered state is a useful abstraction for verifiable humanoid VLA execution.
